requirements.requirement: Nightly backup mechanism (cron job) configured on node1 to run the backup automatically
requirements.summary: /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup.sh created and /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup installed to run it daily at 02:15 as root; cron service confirmed active both before and after node1's restart, showing the schedule persists.

requirements.requirement: Backup transfers /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1
requirements.summary: Script uses rsync over SSH from node2:/srv/inventory/data; a manual run produced an archive on node1 whose contents (warehouse-a.csv, warehouse-b.csv, last-updated.txt) exactly match the files present on node2. Re-validated after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Dated archives stored under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: Archive inventory-2026-09-29.tar.gz was created and confirmed present under /var/backups/inventory using a YYYY-MM-DD naming scheme.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last 7 days of archives
requirements.summary: Executor seeded synthetic archives at ages 7-10 days and 2/5 days, then reran the script: the 7-10 day-old archives were deleted while the 2- and 5-day-old archives survived, directly demonstrating the find -mtime +6 -delete retention window. Test archives were cleaned up afterward, leaving only the legitimate archive.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes of the backup task are directly satisfied with first-party evidence: a nightly cron job invokes an rsync-over-SSH script that pulls node2:/srv/inventory/data into dated tar.gz archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1, and a controlled retention test confirms the 7-day pruning window works exactly as intended. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly for both nodes — pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, boot-identity change, and full recovery of ssh/cron/data/backup-pipeline are all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots, adding confidence though restart survival is not itself part of the public task contract. No unaddressed residue or unnecessary mutations were found; the few test/seed mutations performed were bounded, purposeful, and cleaned up.
limitations: The cron entry's actual nightly (02:15) trigger could not be observed directly within the session window; correctness was instead verified via manual invocation of the same script, which is the standard way to validate cron-driven logic without waiting for the scheduled time.

Data used for the backup content was synthetic sample data created by the executor because /srv/inventory/data did not pre-exist on node2; this does not affect the correctness of the backup mechanism itself.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full command timeline: all state-changing actions map to clear task purposes. Fixing sshd (missing host keys, ssh-keygen -A + restart) on both nodes and enabling/testing SSH access were necessary prerequisites since rsync-over-SSH is the transfer mechanism and sshd was broken in the starting environment. Seeding node2 with sample inventory data (cmd-28385c7d7b2f4593) was a necessary substitute since /srv/inventory/data did not exist, and there was otherwise nothing to back up. Synthetic retention-test archives created via touch -d (cmd-5dcad71e13fa42d0, cmd-bce4ded845a74e0f) were a bounded, low-risk validation technique, and the remaining test archives were explicitly deleted afterward (cmd-e2614d1ac2394c48), leaving no residue. The mandatory sequential node1/node2 restarts are bounded and required by the separate restart-evidence protocol. The fixed lifecycle diff confirms no unexpected residue: only boot-identity, expected systemd-private /tmp entries, and the sshd-now-listening delta are visible between after-prepare and after-executor, with no failed services or package-health regressions.
